text:
joel: Heads up — after the runtime push at ~08:12 we started seeing 2x p95 for seq=128 on rw-open-7b-q traffic. Repro in prod across a few pods.

mira: saw the alert, attaching flamegraph and a tiny profile. looks like kernel_selector picked generic_matmul path instead of quant_fast for a subset of requests.

anya: do we have a shard/driver swap around the time of the push? last time selector fell back when driver didn't advertise quant_capability.

joel: yes, deploy-bot shows a rolling driver restart 08:10-08:11 on the pool. suspect race: cache key namespace rotates on driver reload so autotuner warmed cache later.

perf-bot: perf snapshot: seq=128 cohort before push: mean_tok_ns=1.8k, p95=3.2k. after push: mean_tok_ns=3.4k, p95=6.8k. kernel breakdown: 60% generic_matmul, 35% quant_fast, 5% other.

dominic: interesting — generic_matmul is ~2.0x slower for that seqlen in our bench. why did selector pick it? maybe telemetry reports lower accuracy for quant_fast for this model/epoch and autotuner switched.

mira: checked autotuner logs: it marked quant_fast as "incompatible" for model version 2026-02-11 because of a kernel ABI mismatch reported during init. log: `kernel_probe: quant_fast ABI mismatch: optflags v2 != v1`

anya: that ABI mismatch only shows up when model is loaded with vram_layout=packed. we switched default to packed in the driver restart. so selector saw mismatch and disabled quant path. but that should be transient — cache autotune should re-evaluate.

joel: but here's the kicker: kvcache entries got salted when driver reload happened. persistence rehydrate took ~26s and during that gap autotuner had to rebuild cohort samples -> more generic picks. Also TTL granularity was 1s so many entries expired en-masse during rehydrate.

mira: repro steps to confirm:
```
# simulate driver reload and packed layout
./runtimectl set-driver-layout packed && ./runtimectl restart-driver --pool gpu-pool-3
# run focal load
curl -s -X POST 'https://api.redwood/prod/generate' -d '{\'model\':\'rw-open-7b-q\',\'inputs\':[\'x\'*120] ,\'seqlen\':128}'
```

domin ic: can we avoid mass expiration by shifting ttl bucket to coarse 10s for kvcache during rehydrate window? currently TTL is per-entry with 1s resolution.

anya: proposal: add a short-lived rehydrate mode after driver reload where we set kvcache_ttl_granularity=10s and disable key salting rotation until persistence ack. simpler: use stable namespace for persisted keys and only change salt on explicit migration.

perf-bot: quick sim shows that increasing granularity to 10s during rehydrate reduces p95 spike from 6.8k -> 3.6k and speeds kernel re-selection by ~18s.

joel: next actions: 1) mira to add guard in kernel_probe to avoid disabling quant_fast on ABI minor flag mismatch (dominic to review safety). 2) anya to prototype rehydrate mode (ttl coarsen + stable namespace flag). 3) deploy-bot to add canary that forces packed layout in a single pool to reproduce safely.

mira: I'll start a small PR for the probe loosening and add more verbose probe telemetry so we can see exact mismatch bits.

anya: I'll try the rehydrate toggle as a config flag first, no schema change. if it helps we'll make it automatic on driver_ping.

domin ic: I'll review safety but the risk of false-positive quant disable is higher than letting a slightly mismatched kernel try fast path. we can gate with a slow fallback if execution fails a checksum check.

joel: sounds good. also adding a lightweight dashboard: seqlen-cohort kernel_choice by model-version + driver-layout so we can spot these swings quickly. :eyes:

perf-bot: created perf ticket RF-4512 with attached snapshots and suggested mitigation.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled for gpu-pool-3 at 09:30 UTC. will post status.

anya: note for postmortem: include exact key namespace change: old_ns=kv-v1, new_ns=kv-v1-salted-20260211 and persist delay 26s. we'll prefer namespace-stable-by-default unless explicit migration requested.

joel: thanks team. i'll follow up after the canary and once PRs land. :thumbsup:
